items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: They need to listen to Johnny Hodges and hear the difference between his sound versus a Marshall Royal...

ctx.x: Well that’s my question. What was the difference?

That’s one of the things that I wish would happen again. See because a lot of what I went through personally, like Clifford Brown and different ones, Horace Silver and all, any of the guys you want to name, Donald Byrd or Barry Harris. Any of us that were coming along, we played with the older musicians. It was an apprentice period that you served. Now there is so much industry involvement of record companies wanting to sign people. And then they sign a lot of young people because many of them, they don’t know…

really. And everybody is rushing to get — now they’re able to make their own CDs. And I was talking with some of the people from WBGO-FM in Newark. And they were saying that every week they get flooded with CDs from people they never even heard of. And they put on some of them and they are terrible. But what can you do? People have access to make them. And I think that the albums I’ve made I put a lot of thought into. And this is one of the things I admired about Herbie Hancock when he started doing his thing.…
